nodes.summary: The two allele frequencies sum to one: `p + q = 1`.
nodes.title: The two allele frequencies sum to one

nodes.summary: The gamete law is the allele frequency: `gamete G a = ½ ∑ b, G (a, b) + ½ ∑ b, G (b, a)`, half the expected number of copies of `a` in a parental genotype.
nodes.title: Gamete law equals the allele frequency

nodes.summary: Allele frequencies are conserved under random mating: the gamete law of the offspring equals that of the parents.
nodes.title: Allele frequencies are conserved

nodes.summary: The law of a random gamete of a generation with genotype law `G`: pick a parent from `G`, then one of its two alleles by `transmit`. Its mass at `a` is the frequency of allele `a` (`gamete_apply`).
nodes.title: Law of a random gamete

nodes.summary: The deviation from Hardy–Weinberg proportions vanishes after one generation of random mating, whatever the parental genotype law.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg proportions after one generation of random mating

nodes.summary: The deviation `D = P(AA) - p²` of a biallelic genotype law from Hardy–Weinberg proportions, where `p` is the frequency of allele `A` (`true`).
nodes.title: Deviation from Hardy–Weinberg proportions

nodes.summary: Hardy–Weinberg proportions (Hardy 1908, Weinberg 1908): after one generation of random mating the genotype law is the product `p ⊗ p` of the parental allele frequencies `p = gamete G`.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg proportions

nodes.summary: After one generation of random mating the homozygote `aa` has frequency `q²`.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $q^2$ of the aa homozygote

nodes.summary: After one generation of random mating the (unordered) heterozygote `Aa`, i.e. the two ordered genotypes `(A, a)` and `(a, A)`, has frequency `2pq`.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $2pq$ of the heterozygote

nodes.summary: The Hardy–Weinberg proportions reached after one generation of random mating are a fixed point of random mating.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium

nodes.summary: After one generation of random mating the homozygote `AA` has frequency `p²`.
nodes.title: Hardy–Weinberg frequency $p^2$ of the AA homozygote

nodes.summary: The offspring genotype law under random union of gametes: the maternal and paternal alleles are independent gametes of the parental generation.
nodes.title: Offspring genotype law under random union of gametes

nodes.summary: `transmit g` puts mass `1/2` on each of the two alleles of `g` (mass `1` on `a` for a homozygote `g = (a, a)`).
nodes.title: Allele transmission law of a parental genotype

nodes.summary: Mendel's law of segregation: a parent with genotype `g` transmits its maternal allele `g.1` or its paternal allele `g.2`, each with probability `1/2`.
nodes.title: Mendel's law of segregation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
